name: Push-up
description: A bodyweight horizontal push lowering and pressing the whole body from a plank, the foundation of the pressing patterns.
instructions: Start in a high plank with the hands under the shoulders and the body straight from head to heels.
Lower the chest toward the floor while keeping the body rigid in one line.
Press back up to the start without letting the hips sag or pike.
tips: Keep the ribs down and the glutes braced so the body stays in one straight line.
Lower to a consistent depth each rep rather than cutting the range short.
contraindications: Avoid painful shoulder or wrist ranges.

name: Barbell Bench Press
description: A barbell horizontal press lying on a bench, the primary barbell chest lift.
instructions: Lie on the bench with the feet planted and the shoulder blades pulled back and down.
Unrack the bar and lower it under control to the lower chest.
Press the bar up until the elbows are extended over the chest.
tips: Keep the shoulder blades retracted against the bench throughout the press.
Keep the wrists stacked over the elbows rather than letting the bar drift toward the face.
contraindications: Avoid painful shoulder ranges at the bottom of the press.
Use a spotter or safeties when training near failure.

name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
description: A vertical press of a dumbbell in each hand from the shoulders to overhead, training the shoulders and triceps.
instructions: Sit or stand holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height with the palms facing forward.
Brace the trunk and press the dumbbells overhead until the arms are extended.
Lower the dumbbells back to shoulder height under control.
tips: Keep the ribs down and brace the trunk rather than leaning back to press.
Press the dumbbells slightly together at the top without letting them drift forward.
contraindications: Keep the ribs down rather than overarching the lower back to finish the press.

name: Pull-up
description: A bodyweight vertical pull raising the chest to an overhead bar from a dead hang, the primary bodyweight back exercise.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than the shoulders.
Pull the chest toward the bar by driving the elbows down and back.
Lower under control to a full hang.
tips: Start each rep from a still, fully extended hang rather than a swing.
Lead with the elbows and keep the ribs down instead of kicking the legs to cheat up.
contraindications: Avoid if hanging causes shoulder pain.

name: Barbell Deadlift
description: A hip-hinge pull lifting a barbell from the floor to a standing lockout, the primary posterior-chain strength lift.
instructions: Stand with the bar over the midfoot and the shins close to it.
Hinge down with a flat back and grip the bar just outside the knees.
Brace, then push the floor away to stand tall with the bar, keeping it close to the body.
tips: Take the slack out of the bar and brace hard before the bar leaves the floor.
Keep the bar dragging up the legs rather than drifting away from the body.
contraindications: Avoid rounding the lower back off the floor.
Reduce the load if the back cannot stay flat as the bar breaks the ground.

name: Bodyweight Squat
description: A squat performed without external load, the foundation of every loaded squat variation.
instructions: Stand with the feet around shoulder width and the toes turned slightly out.
Sit the hips down and back until the thighs are at least parallel, keeping the chest tall.
Drive through the whole foot to stand back up.
tips: Let the knees travel out over the toes rather than caving inward.
Reach a depth you can control with a flat back rather than forcing lower.
contraindications: Avoid painful ranges at the knees or hips.
Reduce the depth if the lower back rounds at the bottom.

name: Barbell Back Squat
description: A squat with the barbell racked across the upper back, the primary barbell lower-body strength lift.
instructions: Rack the bar across the upper back, unrack it, and step back with the feet around shoulder width.
Brace the trunk and sit the hips down and back into a controlled squat to depth.
Drive through the midfoot to stand back up.
tips: Keep the bar stacked over the midfoot through the whole rep.
Brace before descending rather than trying to catch the brace at the bottom.
contraindications: Avoid painful ranges at the knees, hips, or lower back.
Reduce the load if the back cannot stay flat at depth.

name: Walking Lunge
description: A travelling unilateral lower-body exercise stepping forward into alternating lunges across the floor.
instructions: Stand tall, then step one foot forward and lower until the back knee approaches the floor.
Drive through the front foot to stand up, bringing the back foot forward.
Step forward into the next lunge with the opposite leg and continue.
tips: Keep the front knee tracking over the foot rather than caving inward.
Take a long enough step that the front shin stays near vertical at the bottom.
contraindications: Avoid painful ranges at the front knee.
Shorten the step if balance is hard to control.

name: Plank
description: An isometric core hold from a braced forearm position, resisting extension of the trunk against gravity.
instructions: Set the elbows under the shoulders and the forearms flat on the floor.
Extend the legs behind and brace the trunk, lifting the hips into line.
Hold a straight line from head to heels for the target time.
tips: Keep the ribs down and the glutes braced so the hips do not sag or pike.
Breathe steadily throughout rather than holding the breath.
contraindications: Avoid letting the lower back sag into extension; keep the trunk braced.

name: Romanian Deadlift
description: A hip hinge lowering a barbell down the legs with the knees nearly fixed, emphasising the hamstrings and glutes.
instructions: Stand tall holding the bar at the front of the thighs with a soft knee bend.
Hinge at the hips, sending them back and letting the bar travel down the legs with a flat back.
Drive the hips forward to stand tall once hamstring tension limits the descent.
tips: Keep the knees fixed in a soft bend rather than turning it into a squat.
Stop lowering when the hamstrings run out of range instead of rounding the back to reach further.
contraindications: Avoid rounding the lower back at the bottom of the hinge.

name: Cable Row
description: A seated horizontal pull drawing a cable handle to the torso, a scalable back builder with constant tension.
instructions: Sit tall at the machine with the feet braced and hold the cable handle with the arms extended.
Pull the handle to the torso, driving the elbows back and squeezing the shoulder blades together.
Return the handle under control until the arms are extended and the lats are stretched.
tips: Drive the elbows back rather than shrugging the shoulders up toward the neck.
Keep the torso upright rather than rowing with a big lean back and forth.
contraindications: Avoid rounding the lower back to reach the extended position.

name: Treadmill Run
description: A running exercise on a treadmill for cardiovascular conditioning at a controlled pace.
instructions: Step onto the treadmill and start walking, then build to a manageable running speed.
Run with relaxed shoulders, an upright posture, and a steady cadence.
Slow the belt to a walk to cool down before stepping off.
tips: Build speed gradually rather than jumping onto a fast-moving belt.
Land under the hips with a quick cadence instead of overstriding out in front.
contraindications: Avoid running through sharp joint pain.
Attach the safety clip so the belt stops if you lose footing.
